family.tagline: Two teachers, one guitar and a Companion Core in the hall.
family.story: Parisa runs an online music school from a desk in the hall. Her partner Kian teaches guitar in the room upstairs. Their timetable, forms and music library sit on one Companion Core.

companion.name: Quince
companion.job: Drafts lesson notices and reschedule messages from what Parisa sends it.
companion.limits: Drafts only. Parisa reads and sends every message.

companion.name: Plum
companion.job: Opens websites in its own browser and fills in the forms Kian asks for.
companion.limits: Fills in forms only. Kian checks and sends every one.

popup.title: Kian carries the parcel inside
popup.body: A parcel waits on the porch steps. Kian carries the Companion Core to the Desk Hall, where Parisa clears the desk.

popup.title: Parisa lays out the pieces
popup.body: Inside: the Companion Core, a power cable, a quick-start guide and a recovery USB drive. Parisa lays each piece on the desk while Kian unfolds the guide.

popup.title: The Core wakes in the hall
popup.body: Kian plugs in the cable and Parisa presses the button. The Core wakes and opens its own Wi-Fi network.

popup.title: Parisa joins it from her phone
popup.body: On her phone's Wi-Fi settings, Parisa joins the Core's own network. Then she chooses the home network from the list.

popup.title: Parisa and Kian pick their apps
popup.body: In the Companion Hub store, Parisa picks Hermes and Kian picks OpenClaw. They add Baikal and Navidrome, then walk away.

beats.capability: an agent that connects to chat apps, email and more from one self-hosted app

popup.title: Quince says good morning
popup.body: From the hall desk, Parisa messages the agent she named Quince. Quince answers from the Core beside her, and the day's lessons begin.
popup.note: Messages pass through the chat service you choose.

say.speaker: parisa
say.text: Good morning, Parisa. Quince here. Which student first?

beats.capability: a small CalDAV and CardDAV server for your calendars and contacts

popup.title: Parisa moves two lessons
popup.body: Two students swap their Thursday slots, and Parisa moves both lessons in her calendar app. Baikal serves the timetable and contacts from the Core.

beats.capability: an agent that connects to chat apps, email and more from one self-hosted app

popup.title: Quince drafts the holiday notices
popup.body: Three lessons move for a holiday. Parisa messages Quince the new times, and Quince drafts a note for each student. Parisa reads each one and sends it herself.
popup.note: Messages pass through the chat service you choose.

say.speaker: parisa
say.text: Three drafts, one for each student. Each is yours to read and send.

beats.capability: store every password in a vault you host

popup.title: Sign-ins leave the paper notebook
popup.body: While Kian reads the sign-ins aloud from a paper notebook, Parisa saves each one in VaultWarden. The vault runs on the Core and works with the Bitwarden apps.

beats.capability: back up, search and organise your family photos and videos

popup.title: Parisa searches for the sea
popup.body: On the couch after lunch, Parisa searches Immich for the sea, and the holiday appears. Immich sorted the pictures on the Core, where both their phones back them up.
popup.note: The first start takes a while, because Immich sorts the photos.

beats.capability: stream your own movies, shows and music to every screen in the house

popup.title: Kian picks a concert film
popup.body: On a slow Sunday afternoon, Kian picks a concert film from their own collection. Jellyfin plays it from the Core to the living-room TV.

beats.capability: build forms with logic and file uploads, then collect the answers

popup.title: Parisa builds the trial lesson form
popup.body: At the kitchen counter, Parisa builds a trial lesson form in OpnForm, with a question for each instrument. The answers are collected on the Core.
popup.note: A form shared with the public needs outside access to the Core.

beats.capability: a shared household hub with a recipe book and an expiry tracker

popup.title: Kian writes down his aunt's stew
popup.body: His aunt never wrote the herb stew down. Kian types it into the HomeHub recipe book. The Core keeps it beside the shopping list.

beats.capability: scan and file your paperwork; it reads every page, tags it and makes it searchable

popup.title: Parisa files the insurer's letter
popup.body: At the round table, Parisa scans the insurer's letter and a repair receipt into Paperless-ngx. The Core reads and tags both, so next year one word finds them.

beats.capability: a shared household hub with a recipe book and an expiry tracker

popup.title: Parisa plans meals around spinach
popup.body: Spinach and two tubs of yoghurt are nearly out of date. Parisa spots them on the HomeHub expiry list, kept on the Core, and plans the week's meals around them.

beats.capability: send a push notification to your phone from any script or automation

popup.title: A note arrives before the lesson
popup.body: Coffee in hand on the deck, Parisa feels her phone buzz with a ntfy note. A small script on the Core sends one ahead of each lesson.
popup.note: On an iPhone, ntfy relays the push through an upstream server.

beats.capability: track your plants, watering and care history, with a garden journal

popup.title: Kian keeps a flower journal
popup.body: Between two Saturday lessons, Kian waters the orange flowers by the back deck and notes it in HortusFox. Each watering goes into a journal on the Core.

beats.capability: edit audio in a browser tab: cut, fade, normalise, export

popup.title: Kian trims the chord change
popup.body: Morning light reaches the guitar stand. Kian records a chord change for Friday's lesson. He trims it in AudioMass, served from the Core in a browser tab.

beats.capability: the Obsidian note app in your browser; notes stay as local Markdown files

popup.title: Kian plans a week of lessons
popup.body: From the lounge chair, Kian writes next week's lesson plan in Obsidian. It runs in a browser session, and the notes are plain Markdown files on the Core.

beats.capability: plan tasks and time blocks in one local file on your Core

popup.title: Parisa gives admin its own blocks
popup.body: Seated on the cushioned bench, Parisa blocks out the term's admin hours in Companion Planning. It is one local file on the Core. Reports and enrolment each get a slot.
popup.note: Crash reports go to Companion Intelligence unless switched off.

beats.capability: stream your own music collection to any device

popup.title: Kian warms up on the bed
popup.body: Before the first student, Kian sits on the bed and plays along to a backing track. Navidrome streams his own music folder from the Core to his phone.

beats.capability: errands and browser automation on your Core, prepared for you to approve

popup.title: Plum fills in the string order
popup.body: The old strings have gone dull. Kian asks Plum to open the supplier's website and fill in the order form. He checks every field and sends it himself.
popup.note: OpenClaw reaches websites over your home internet.

say.speaker: kian
say.text: The order form is filled in. The address is the field to check.

popup.title: One Core, one small school
popup.body: Timetable, forms, drafts and music run on one Companion Core, in the hall of a modern house.

closing.body: Your lesson calendar, forms and music can run on a Companion Core at home. Browse the Companion Hub store and pick your first apps.

notes: The Core stands on the only desk, in the Desk Hall. Parisa's office beats anchor on the Core or the hall; no second desk is named. Kian's room has a guitar stand, bed, cushioned bench and lounge chair; no screen, so no beat names one.
kitchen-intake: OpnForm carries the public-access caveat as a note. The beat never says how students reach the form, and no remote access is claimed.
Hermes (Quince) is Parisa's; OpenClaw (Plum) is Kian's. Every agent beat has the person read and send. The OpenClaw website note rides on bed-strings.
Companion Planning and the two agents send crash reports to Companion Intelligence unless switched off; office-term carries that note and nothing says that nothing leaves the Core.
garden-ntfy: the iPhone relay caveat from the ntfy listing is in the note. The reminder script is a small script on the Core, not an app feature the listing promises.

No Companion Memory, no Steam, no code host. AudioMass is described only as a browser-tab editor served from the Core; no beat says recordings are stored on the Core. Film: eight beats, both members, six chapters, one small-business beat.
